title: Late Breaking Results: Multi-Objective Multi-Bit Flip-Flop Placement Considering Pre-Placed Cells
problem: Clustering single-bit flip-flops into multi-bit flip-flops reduces power and area but causes excessive displacement during legalization that degrades timing, especially with pre-placed cells in the design.
motivation: Multi-bit flip-flop clustering is a proven power/area optimization, but timing degradation from displacement limits adoption; pre-placed cells exacerbate the problem.
method: The approach uses physics-inspired forces to reposition flip-flops (memory elements) to reduce timing problems. It combines clustering (grouping single-bit flip-flops into multi-bit units) and legalization (fixing placement violations), making them work together to minimize damage from moving things around. A scoring system that balances multiple competing goals—timing performance, power consumption, chip area, and efficient bin usage—determines which flip-flops to group.
key_novelty: It's the first MBFF placement method that explicitly accounts for pre-placed cells (circuit elements locked in fixed positions) during clustering and legalization while simultaneously optimizing timing, power, chip area, and bin utilization.
contributions: Force-based flip-flop relocation model to mitigate timing violations
Integrated clustering and legalization to reduce displacement-induced timing degradation
Multi-objective function for candidate selection across timing, power, area, and utilization
Demonstrated CAD Contest victory on ICCAD 2024 Power and Timing track

metrics.other: Won 2024 CAD Contest at ICCAD on Power and Timing Optimization Using Multi-Bit Flip-Flops

baselines: Other participating teams in ICCAD 2024 CAD Contest
limitations: Not discussed in abstract; evaluation limited to contest benchmarks.
primary_theme: MBFF placement with pre-placed cell handling and multi-objective timing/power/area trade-off
